blocks.x: October Prime Day always throws up some great deals sooner or later, but holy moly have good prices on gaming laptops been hard to find this year. Both in terms of machines I can recommend for their value, and stock in general. Most RTX 5060 lappys are now priced the same as RTX 5070 machines in 2025, and I guess we all have to get used to that fact.
Anyway, I've rounded up the six gaming laptop deals I'd stand behind for under $1,500, saving you the trouble of sorting through the listings yourself.
We're curating all the best Prime Day PC gaming deals here

I spend hours every week hunting for the best discounts on gaming laptops, and the rest of the year testing them. Each of these machines has genuine merit for the price in this topsy-turvy market, and gets the PC Gamer seal of approval for being better than the rest.

Oh, and my personal highlight? It's this Acer Nitro V 16 with an 85 W RTX 5070 mobile for $1,200 at Amazon. Try as I might, I can't beat it in terms of the gaming grunt you get for your cash. But all of the lappys below represent great value compared to the rest right now—so let's see what we've got, shall we?

The deals in full

LOQ | RTX 5050 (100 W) | 16 GB DDR5: was $1174.99 now $998.99
Ordinarily, an RTX 5050 gaming laptop for nearly $1,000 wouldn't be particularly special. However, this one has a 100 W GPU power limit, which means it should be reasonably punchy when paired with a 1080p display. It's a shame the RAM is limited to a single module, but in terms of gaming performance the lack of dual channel shouldn't affect it much, as we found when we reviewed an RTX 5060 model late last year.
Key specs: RTX 5050 (100 W) | Core i5 13450HX | 15-inch | 1080p | 144 Hz | 16 GB DDR5 | 512 GBView Deal

Nitro V 16 | RTX 5060 (75 W) | 16 GB DDR5: was $1629.99 now $1149.99
If you're shopping for a gaming laptop anywhere near the $1,000 mark, SSD sizes can unfortunately suffer. This Acer lappy has a 512 GB model, which is pretty small, and the GPU's 75 W power limit is a touch low. However, it's still the cheapest (good) RTX 5060 gaming laptop I can find, and it should perform well with its 1200p, 165 Hz screen. If you're watching your pennies, this is a good price for this particular machine.
Key specs: RTX 5060 (75 W) | Core 7 240H | 16-inch | 1200p | 165 Hz | 16 GB DDR5 | 512 GB SSDView Deal

Nitro V 16 | RTX 5070 (85 W) | 16 GB DDR5: was $1299.99 now $1199.99
Good lord, it's an RTX 5070 gaming laptop for the same price I used to find them. This Acer Nitro V 16 is a solidly specced machine, what with its 10-core Intel CPU (six Performance, four Efficient) and Nvidia's mid-range graphics card sitting in its tidy-looking frame. The GPU has been power limited to 85 W, but it should still do very well with a 1200p screen. It's a shame about the small SSD, but for this price, in this market? I'll take it all day long.
Key specs: RTX 5070 (85 W) | Core 7 240H | 16-inch | 1200p | 180 Hz | 16 GB DDR5 | 512 GB SSDView Deal

Aero X16 | RTX 5060 (85 W) | 32 GB DDR5: was $1299.99 now $1224.99
This is a power-limited RTX 5060 machine—but you do get 32 GB of DDR5 for your cash, which is increasingly rare in 2026. The processor is decently beefy, too, although you will need to lean on upscaling to make the most of its 1600p 165 Hz screen. If you want 32 GB of RAM in a gaming laptop, this is about the cheapest I'd consider.
Key specs: RTX 5060 (85 W) | Ryzen AI 7 350 | 16-inch | 1600p | 165 Hz | 32 GB DDR5 | 1 TB SSDView Deal

Nitro V 16S | RTX 5070 (85 W) | 16 GB DDR5: was $1649.99 now $1401.99
This is one of the cheapest RTX 5070 machines we can find right now that we'd actually want to buy ourselves. It comes with a modern AMD Ryzen AI 7 350 chip, 180 Hz 16-inch IPS display, 1 TB SSD, and 16 GB of DDR5. We've seen a few RTX 5070 laptops going for less over recent months but right now, this is one of the best in terms of value. Especially as it's the slim Nitro design, which should slip pretty easily into a reasonably-sized backpack.
Key specs: RTX 5070 (85 W) | Ryzen AI 7 350 | 16-inch | 1600p | 180 Hz | 16 GB DDR5 | 1 TB SSDView Deal

Legion 5i | RTX 5060 (100 W) | 16 GB DDR5 | OLED: was $2299.99 now $1499
While this is still a lot of money for an RTX 5060 machine, there are two main points to consider. One, it's got a 100 W GPU power limit, which is better than most. And two, it's got a 165 Hz OLED display, which means you get some of the best screen tech around crammed within a 15.1 inch frame. The CPU is plenty punchy, and it's also got a proper 1 TB SSD. The RTX 5060 will need a fair bit of DLSS help to push pixels at 1600p resolution, but this lappy is still well worth considering for the cash.
Key specs: RTX 5060 (100 W) | Core i7 14700HX | 15.1-inch | 1600p | 165 Hz OLED | 16 GB DDR5 | 1 TB SSDView Deal
